Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage overnight is dominated by the aftershocks of the Democratic midterm sweep, with nearly every outlet dissecting the historic AI/tech stock selloff and growing political backlash against data centers. Secondary threads include fallout from Stephen Miller's elevation to White House chief of staff, Anthropic's big energy deal, and corporate tax and crypto scrutiny stories from the FT and NYT.

stories.headline: AI stock rout deepens as Democrats' data-center backlash spooks Wall Street
stories.summary: Tech and chip stocks suffered their worst slide since the pandemic after Democratic wins in Texas, Ohio and Georgia put anti-data-center governors in office, with the Nasdaq Composite falling 5.5% and the SOX semiconductor index posting its worst day since 2020; stocks were recovering some losses by Friday.

stories.headline: Anthropic strikes $3.4bn deal to generate gas-fired power for data centres
stories.summary: Anthropic is bypassing traditional power suppliers in a $3.4 billion deal to secure scarce gas-fired generation equipment as data-center energy demand surges amid the broader AI buildout crunch.

stories.headline: Apple saves $2.7bn in taxes by booking profits in Singapore
stories.summary: New disclosures show Singapore has overtaken Ireland as Apple's largest tax shelter, saving the iPhone maker billions as it shifts profit booking strategies.

stories.headline: Stephen Miller's promotion to chief of staff angers industries reliant on immigrant labor
stories.summary: Trump's naming of the deportation architect as chief of staff has triggered anger and fear among business leaders in industries dependent on immigrant workers, and is deepening GOP soul-searching after the midterm wipeout.

stories.headline: U.S. cleared Nvidia chips to Chinese firms with empty offices and troubling ties
stories.summary: The Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips, some of which reportedly have ties to firms already under U.S. sanctions over national security concerns.

stories.headline: Crypto industry braces for reckoning over Trump family ties
stories.summary: Democrats have vowed to open investigations into President Trump's family crypto dealings after their sweeping midterm victory, putting the industry on edge.

stories.headline: Tesla to wind down Cybertruck production as Musk pivots to Cybercab
stories.summary: Musk confirmed Tesla will end Cybertruck production in Texas next year to make room for the autonomous Cybercab, after the polarizing vehicle failed to reach mass-market sales despite several recalls.

stories.headline: Meta's $25 billion bond sale highlights shifting landscape for tech debt
stories.summary: Meta's decision to sell billions in corporate bonds on Election Day is being read as a test of investor appetite for tech debt amid growing scrutiny of AI capital spending.

Business.gaps: Puck had no business-relevant items surfaced in search or feed.

US politics.overview: Coverage across political outlets is dominated by the fallout from Democrats' historic midterm sweep of Congress, with the biggest story being Trump's decision to replace chief of staff Susie Wiles with hardliner Stephen Miller. Outlets are also digging into the GOP's internal reckoning, Democrats' plans to use their new majorities on tariffs, Medicaid and investigations, and lingering Iran-related tensions.

stories.headline: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff
stories.summary: Axios reports Trump, angered over midterm losses, replaced Wiles with Stephen Miller, a hardliner on immigration and the Iran war, in a move seen as doubling down rather than moderating after the GOP's defeat.

stories.headline: GOP grapples with 'historic defeat' and whether a reckoning is coming
stories.summary: Politico reports that Stephen Miller's elevation to chief of staff has deepened Republican fears that the party will not undergo a broader strategic reckoning after its midterm wipeout.

stories.headline: Democrats plan to target Trump's tariffs now that they control Congress
stories.summary: The Hill reports Democrats are preparing to challenge President Trump's tariffs directly as part of a broader push to lower living costs after their midterm wins.

stories.headline: Trump says 'a few' cabinet changes are coming after GOP's midterm blowout
stories.summary: The Hill reports Trump indicated he will make limited cabinet changes following Republicans' heavy midterm losses to Democrats.

stories.headline: Dana White says he'll meet Trump Monday over offer to be White House press secretary
stories.summary: NPR reports UFC CEO Dana White, a longtime Trump ally, confirmed he will meet with the president Monday after Trump said he offered him the White House press secretary job.

stories.headline: Sotomayor says she hopes Supreme Court will overturn presidential immunity ruling
stories.summary: The Hill reports Justice Sonia Sotomayor said she hopes the Court's decision granting former presidents broad criminal immunity will eventually be reversed, calling some of her colleagues' reasoning troubling.

stories.headline: Democrats will hold their largest number of state legislative trifectas since 1984
stories.summary: Stateline reports a new analysis shows sweeping Democratic gains in state legislatures alongside their congressional wins, giving the party unusually broad control heading into 2027.

stories.headline: US military fires on cargo ship in Gulf of Oman amid Iran tensions
stories.summary: The Hill reports a U.S. military aircraft disabled a commercial vessel in the Gulf of Oman, the latest escalation in the ongoing conflict with Iran that many Republicans blame for midterm losses.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS had no fresh 48-hour items on this topic in search results (its most relevant piece was dated from August); Cook Political Report's most recent original analysis found was from late October/pre-election, with no new post-election piece surfacing in search.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage this cycle is dominated by the fallout from the US midterms for the AI industry — voters punishing data-center buildouts and investors souring on frontier-AI valuations — alongside a cluster of stories about US-China chip security, a major crypto-adjacent hack, and Tesla's retreat from the Cybertruck.

stories.headline: Midterm backlash against data centers reshapes AI industry's political outlook
stories.summary: 404 Media reports that data centers were explicitly on the ballot in more than 40 races across 13 states and people voted against them in 38, with six cities banning them outright and Texas's pro-data-center governor losing his seat. TechCrunch and MIT Technology Review both describe how Democratic control of Congress and several governorships could bring new moratoriums, power-cost rules and community-approval requirements, while OpenAI and Meta executives are publicly bracing for a tougher buildout environment.

stories.headline: Anthropic's IPO valuation cut sharply as tech selloff hits roadshow
stories.summary: The Decoder reports Anthropic is pressing ahead with a pre-Thanksgiving IPO at a valuation of $1.25 to $1.75 trillion, down from a previously hoped-for $2 trillion, as the post-midterm selloff hits AI stocks. Bloomberg separately reported that some prospective buyers are discussing a valuation as low as $1.1 trillion to $1.3 trillion.

stories.headline: OpenAI completes funding round at reduced $1.25 trillion valuation
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports OpenAI closed an $11 billion funding tranche at a $1.25 trillion valuation, a marked reduction in its fundraising ambitions that reflects shifting sentiment around AI spending and new data-center uncertainty after the midterms.

stories.headline: US cleared Nvidia chip sales to Chinese firms with empty offices and sanctioned ties
stories.summary: The New York Times reports the Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia's H200 chips despite some having ties to sanctioned firms, raising questions about vetting. The Verge separately flagged that neither Commerce nor Nvidia appear to be doing adequate due diligence on the Chinese buyers being cleared.

stories.headline: US intelligence memo alleges China recruited exec to spy on Nvidia's CEO
stories.summary: TechCrunch reports a memo circulated earlier this year claimed China's Ministry of State Security recruited a female technology executive at Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

stories.headline: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
stories.summary: Ars Technica reports the crypto-tracing firm disclosed a 'multifront cyberattack' involving AI agents and an on-path data-snatching technique that compromised credentials and tokens across its entire customer base.

stories.headline: Tesla winding down Cybertruck production after election backlash
stories.summary: The Verge notes Elon Musk declared via tweet that Tesla will wind down Cybertruck production next year, timing that follows the midterm backlash against Musk and the data-center industry covered in TechCrunch's post-midterm analysis.

stories.headline: Apple saved $2.7bn in taxes by routing profits through Singapore
stories.summary: The Financial Times reports new disclosures show Singapore has overtaken Ireland as Apple's biggest tax shelter, saving the iPhone maker $2.7 billion this year by routing up to $50 billion in profits through the city-state.

Tech & AI.gaps: Platformer, VentureBeat, Rest of World, Google DeepMind had no clearly dated last-24-48h stories found via search; The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist and The Guardian were assessed only via their provided feed items since they block web search.

Energy.overview: Energy and climate outlets are dominated by fallout from the US midterms, where data center backlash and ratepayer anger reshaped state and federal energy politics, alongside a fresh wave of utility capital-spending plans tied to AI-driven load growth. Secondary threads include a big AI-gas power deal, California grid and rate-hike controversies, and China's dominance in global energy investment.

stories.headline: Midterm 'blue wave' driven by data center and utility bill backlash reshapes energy policy
stories.summary: Latitude Media reports that Democratic wins in Texas, Ohio, Wisconsin and Michigan were driven largely by candidates running against data centers and utility rate hikes, with new governors pledging moratoriums, renewable-only requirements, and cost-shifting rules onto developers. Heatmap similarly argues the midterms marked the end of Trump's fossil-fuel-first energy politics and the rise of a more moderate, affordability-focused Democratic energy coalition skeptical of AI data centers.

stories.headline: Anthropic strikes $3.4bn deal to generate gas-fired power for data centers
stories.summary: FT reports the AI lab is bypassing traditional power suppliers in a bid to lock up scarce turbine and generation equipment as data center energy demand surges.

stories.headline: US utilities keep ramping up capex on data center-driven load growth
stories.summary: Duke Energy says its 15.4 GW large-load pipeline and $103 billion gas-heavy spending plan are unchanged post-election, while Sempra expects a 20% increase to Oncor's capital plan and DTE is expanding its five-year investment plan 30% after selling its unregulated Vantage subsidiary to fund growth.

stories.headline: Senate permitting deal's odds worsen after midterms
stories.summary: Heatmap reports the outlook for passing the bipartisan Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act permitting deal in the lame-duck session grew shakier after the midterms, with clean energy Democrats like John Podesta and Rep. Sean Casten raising objections even as the Senate is slated to vote around November 9.

stories.headline: PG&E's $2 billion grid spending cutbacks threaten California's clean energy buildout
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that PG&E's wildfire-liability-driven grid spending cuts risk stalling solar and storage interconnections and could force the state to delay retiring aging coastal gas plants, posing a challenge for California's incoming governor.

stories.headline: Berkshire Hathaway utility seeks historic 57% rate hike in California
stories.summary: WSJ reports Pacific Power is asking California regulators for a rate increase that would add about $120 a month to the typical residential power bill.

stories.headline: China set to lead world in energy investment in 2026
stories.summary: Bloomberg, citing state broadcaster CCTV, reports China is projected to invest $940 billion in energy in 2026, more than any other country, according to a report from a state-linked enterprise research group.

stories.headline: US solar manufacturing booms at the panel stage but lags on cells and polysilicon
stories.summary: Canary Media's Julian Spector finds US factories can already produce more finished solar panels than needed to meet last year's 47.9 GW of installations, but upstream cell, wafer and polysilicon production remains a weak spot as federal tax credits wind down.

Energy.gaps: E&E News and Argus Media had no verifiable coverage from the last 48 hours in available results; The Economist's climate newsletter item and NYT/Reuters were limited to the single feed items provided, with no additional searchable confirmation since those outlets block search.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage across Chinese, Taiwanese and international outlets this week centers on the run-up to the APEC summit in Shenzhen (Nov 18-19), with intense focus on a possible historic Xi-Trump-Putin trilateral meeting and renewed US-China trade friction over rare earths and farm purchases. Cross-strait tensions are also prominent, with Taiwan closing its Papua New Guinea office and reports of Chinese military activity simulating a Taiwan blockade, while business coverage highlights China's energy investment dominance, a global AI-stock slump reviving interest in Chinese equities, and new US scrutiny of Nvidia chip flows to Chinese firms.

stories.headline: China confirms plans for Xi-Trump-Putin meeting
stories.summary: Beijing's foreign ministry has for the first time confirmed it is in communication with Washington and Moscow about an unprecedented trilateral meeting between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Shenzhen APEC summit, though analysts say it would likely be more symbolic photo-op than substantive negotiation.

stories.headline: Top US, China officials raise trade 'concerns' as APEC approaches
stories.summary: US and Chinese officials held tense trade talks ahead of the APEC summit, with Washington pressing Beijing to deliver on rare-earth and agricultural purchase commitments under a trade truce set to expire in January, while China's commerce ministry says further farm purchases hinge on reciprocal tariff cuts.

stories.headline: Taiwan says it closes representative office in Papua New Guinea, blames China
stories.summary: Taiwan announced it is shutting its representative office in Papua New Guinea and withdrawing staff, attributing the move to Chinese coercion of the South Pacific nation.

stories.headline: PLA may be simulating Taiwan isolation: report
stories.summary: Taipei Times reports concerns that China's People's Liberation Army may be rehearsing an isolation or blockade scenario against Taiwan, part of a cluster of front-page security stories including rising concern over Chinese overseas policing activity.

stories.headline: U.S. Cleared Nvidia Chips to Chinese Firms With Empty Offices and Troubling Ties
stories.summary: The US Commerce Department approved dozens of Chinese companies to receive Nvidia's H200 chips despite some having ties to entities already under national-security sanctions, raising fresh questions about export-control enforcement.

stories.headline: China Set to Lead World in Energy Investment in 2026, CCTV Says
stories.summary: China is projected to invest about $940 billion in energy in 2026, more than any other country, according to a report released by state broadcaster CCTV-linked China Enterprise Reform group — a state-run assessment underscoring Beijing's push for energy-sector dominance.

stories.headline: China Raises Delegate Count to 2,360 for 2027 Party Congress
stories.summary: China has set a quota of 2,360 delegates for the Communist Party's 21st national congress in 2027, an increase of 60 from the previous gathering, according to state news agency Xinhua.

stories.headline: AI Slump Revives Asia's Forgotten Trades From China to India
stories.summary: A post-midterms unwinding of the global AI trade is pushing investors back toward previously out-of-favor Chinese and Indian stocks as they rethink their regional investment strategies.

China.gaps: Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Global Times, China Daily, Xinhua, CGTN, Yicai Global, TechNode, and Focus Taiwan had no clearly dated, on-topic stories surfaced in the last 24-48 hours via available search and feed items. Reuters, AP, FT, WSJ and The Economist block search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Gulf and Middle East outlets are dominated by a sharp escalation in the Yemen-Saudi war, with a Houthi strike damaging an Aramco building in Riyadh's financial district, alongside parallel flashpoints over Iran (US blockade enforcement, tanker fires in the Strait of Hormuz) and Israel's post-election coalition drama as Gadi Eisenkot gets the mandate to try to unseat Netanyahu. Economic coverage centers on a landmark GCC railway pact and signs that Saudi Arabia's war-hit economy is stabilizing, while Gaza's flooding crisis adds a humanitarian dimension.

stories.headline: Houthi missiles hit Riyadh, damaging Aramco tower in financial district
stories.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles fired by Yemen's Houthis toward Riyadh on Sunday, while an Aramco administrative building in the King Abdullah Financial District was damaged by falling debris, marking a major escalation in the war's reach into the Saudi capital with no casualties reported.

stories.headline: Herzog taps Eisenkot, Netanyahu's rival, to form Israel's next government
stories.summary: Israel's president gave Yashar leader Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to try to build a coalition after a deadlocked election, with Eisenkot securing 67 recommendations to Netanyahu's 46, though his path to a governing majority remains fraught with ultra-Orthodox and Arab-party complications.

stories.headline: US military disables vessel breaking Iran blockade as tankers ablaze in Hormuz
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said three tankers travelling an unauthorized route in the Strait of Hormuz were hit by explosions and fires, a day after a US military aircraft fired on and disabled a commercial vessel attempting to break Washington's naval blockade of Iran.

stories.headline: Houthi-run health ministry says Saudi strikes killed 33 near Sanaa
stories.summary: Yemen's Houthi-run Saba news agency said Saudi-led coalition air strikes killed at least 33 people and wounded dozens more in a village near Sanaa, a claim Saudi authorities said they were investigating.

stories.headline: GCC states sign landmark agreement to advance Gulf railway project
stories.summary: An agreement on the mega rail project linking all six GCC members—Saudi Arabia, the UAE, Oman, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain—was signed in Bahrain's capital, setting a joint framework for implementing and operating the cross-border network.

stories.headline: Saudi GDP contraction slows as economy shows partial recovery from war disruption
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia's real GDP fell 3.8% year-on-year in the third quarter, an improvement from a 4.7% drop in Q2, with non-oil activity rising even as oil output remained down 20% amid continued war-related shipping disruptions.

stories.headline: Floods swamp tens of thousands of tents in Gaza as heavy rain hits region
stories.summary: Heavy rains killed two people in Iraq and inundated tens of thousands of makeshift shelters in Gaza, leaving displaced Palestinian families wading through rainwater that has flooded their tents.

stories.headline: Bahrain to restore envoy to Baghdad after first Iraqi PM visit in decades
stories.summary: Bahrain announced it will restore its ambassador to Baghdad following a breakthrough visit by Iraq's prime minister, the first such trip in decades, signaling warming diplomatic ties between Manama and Baghdad.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: Arab News, Khaleej Times (beyond the railway story), Arabian Business, Saudi Gazette, Al Arabiya English, Ynetnews, Haaretz, Asharq Al-Awsat (beyond items in search snippet), and Iran International (beyond the Aramco liveblog) did not yield additional distinct recent stories beyond what is reflected above; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT and BBC were not independently searchable and are not represented beyond any overlap with feed items.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by two major democracy stories out of East and Southern Africa: Tanzania's Tundu Lissu verdict and South Africa's municipal elections, alongside economic policy debates in Ethiopia and major investment deals in Nigeria and Namibia.

stories.headline: Tanzania's Lissu cleared of treason but jailed four years for incitement
stories.summary: Opposition leader Tundu Lissu avoided the death penalty when a Dar es Salaam court acquitted him of treason but convicted him of incitement and sentenced him to four years, a verdict he called political persecution; Africanews, Al Jazeera and Africa Confidential also covered the case and the wider crackdown on Chadema following last year's disputed election.

stories.headline: South Africa's ANC heads to record-low vote share in municipal polls
stories.summary: With most ballots counted the ANC was on track for its worst-ever municipal election result as opposition parties made urban gains, a story also tracked by Africanews and Africa Confidential, which framed it as deepening fragmentation within Ramaphosa's coalition.

stories.headline: Ethiopia's rebased $201bn economy brings a bigger tax bill, not easier borrowing
stories.summary: Addis Ababa's statistical rebasing confirms Ethiopia as sub-Saharan Africa's third-largest economy, but economists say it mainly expands the tax base while security risks and renewed fighting threaten Abiy Ahmed's investment push, a tension Africa Confidential also highlighted this week.

stories.headline: Namibia's president takes personal charge of Dangote's $2.5bn fuel project
stories.summary: President Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah said she will personally oversee Dangote's fuel storage and regional pipeline investment to avoid bureaucratic delays costing Namibia another major project.

stories.headline: Nigeria's NNPC plans IPO stake sale
stories.summary: State-run Africa Confidential's Pointers column reports that state oil company NNPC is preparing to offer a 5-10% stake in an initial public offering as part of its commercialisation drive.

Africa.gaps: Could not retrieve recent Reuters, AP, BBC, FT, NYT or WSJ coverage beyond the single WSJ trophy-hunting feed item, as these outlets block search; The Continent had no distinct recent items beyond its general subscription page.

Media.overview: Media trade press is dominated by post-midterms fallout: how newsrooms and streamers covered election night, Fox's completed $22 billion Roku acquisition, and advertiser backlash against podcasters over a Charlie Kirk joke. Several outlets are also tracking The New York Times' high-stakes AI copyright case against OpenAI and Microsoft, plus press-freedom and journalism-ethics stories from the UK and Russia.

stories.headline: Fox Corp. Completes $22 Billion Acquisition of Roku
stories.summary: Fox closed its $22 billion purchase of Roku, folding the streaming platform into Fox Digital Platforms alongside Tubi and Fox One, creating what Adweek calls the third-largest entity in U.S. TV by viewing share.

stories.headline: What Could the Times Buy With Its A.I. Bucks?
stories.summary: Puck reports that The New York Times' copyright lawsuit against OpenAI and Microsoft is nearing a decisive phase, with legal experts telling Puck the paper is positioned for a settlement that could run into ten figures and reshape licensing across the industry.

stories.headline: 'I've Had It' Podcasters Apologize for 'Insensitive' Charlie Kirk Joke as Advertisers Cut Ties
stories.summary: Hosts Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan apologized after laughing at a meme mocking the assassinated conservative organizer, as sponsors including Cash App and Chewy pulled their support.

stories.headline: Children of the Kornacki: How NBC's Election Livestream Beat the Creator Economy
stories.summary: Puck details how NBC's 10.5-hour "Kornacki Cam" livestream drew 29 million views across platforms and out-dueled streamers like Hasan Piker, showing legacy TV news still anchors the fragmented digital-election ecosystem.

stories.headline: Newsmax's Trump Troubles
stories.summary: Status reports that Nielsen data it obtained shows the pro-Trump network Newsmax is losing audience even as it positioned itself as MAGA's loudest media voice, raising questions about its next move.

stories.headline: Trump Asks UFC Chief Dana White to Be His New Press Secretary
stories.summary: Trump reportedly floated UFC boss Dana White for the open White House press secretary job; White has not formally accepted and later reportedly turned the offer down.

stories.headline: Novaya Gazeta's Journalism Will Live On
stories.summary: CJR reports that Russia's storied independent outlet Novaya Gazeta is shutting down permanently on November 9 after being labeled a "foreign agent," but a PEN America-backed project called Kronika is digitizing its full archive to preserve it.

stories.headline: Journalism Came Under Attack During Brand Trial and Was Vindicated by Guilty Verdict
stories.summary: Press Gazette covers how reporters faced hostility during the trial, including a defence barrister swearing at a Sunday Times reporter outside court, before the guilty verdict was seen as affirming the journalism behind the case.

Media.gaps: No recent coverage found from Nieman Lab, Poynter, Digiday, Mediaite, WSJ, FT, Bloomberg, NYT or The Guardian specifically on media-industry topics beyond what's listed; NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block web search so only feed items could be used for them.
